slides.eyebrow: Can I fit it around work?
slides.h: Online study, plus studio days.
body: Teacher Training uses blended learning: online study, plus in-person training days and practice here at the studio.
Mat + Anatomy runs 15 to 16 January 2027. Reformer + Special Populations also starts in January.

slides.h: Our Master Trainer, Simone.
body: Diploma-qualified since 2016, with years of teaching on the Sunshine Coast. She joined Club Pilates in 2025 and became a Master Trainer.

slides.h: Part of a bigger pathway.
body: January's Mat, Reformer, Anatomy and Special Populations modules are part of the Club Pilates teacher training pathway: 500 hours in full.

slides.h: Starts January 2027.
body: Wondering if you have enough experience? Tell us about your Pilates so far and we'll talk it through.

slides.h: Grip socks and comfy clothes. That's all you need.
body: Book through the link in bio.

slides.h: The Wunda chair. Small, and deceptively hard.
body: A padded box with a spring-loaded pedal. It asks for balance, strength and control, and you'll meet it in our classes.

slides.h: Your toes do more than you think.
body: Toe grip socks give each toe space to spread and align, and Restore helps release tight feet.
Ask about toe grip socks at the front desk.

slides.h: Moving up a level? Your instructor will say when.
body: Level 2 Evolution needs Level 1.5 experience and your instructor's go-ahead. Level 2.5 Mastery needs Level 2 experience and the same go-ahead.
No rush.

slides.h: The Pilates ball. Small, soft, surprisingly useful.
body: You'll see it in class on the reformer, the Wunda chair and the springboard, for support, release and a little extra challenge.

slides.h: Tell us it's your first class. We'll take it from there.
body: Let the front desk and your instructor know when you arrive, and they'll help you set up and settle in.

slides.h: Reformer, Wunda chair, springboard. All three, all here.
body: We're a fully equipped Pilates studio, and our classes use all of them.

slides.h: Clothes you can move in. Socks with grip.
body: Comfortable activewear works well. Grip socks are required in every class, and we sell them at the front desk.

slides.h: Level 1 Foundations: start here, stay as long as you like.
body: Where everyone starts: the equipment, the basics and plenty of options to modify. Made for first-timers.
slides.cta: Find it on the schedule, link in bio.

slides.h: Restore: for tight, tired muscles.
body: Myofascial release on the equipment. A slower class that works into tight, tired muscles, then moves you through them. Suits anyone who wants a slower session in their week.
slides.cta: Find it on the schedule, link in bio.

slides.h: Reformer Flow: keep it moving.
body: Reformer-based Pilates with a contemporary flow. Good if you like a class that keeps moving from one exercise to the next.
slides.cta: Find it on the schedule, link in bio.

slides.h: Level 1.5 Progression: the next step.
body: More complex movement and stability work. For when the Level 1 basics feel familiar.
slides.cta: Find it on the schedule, link in bio.

slides.h: The springboard: Pilates, standing up.
body: Springs on the wall for standing, arm and leg work against resistance. For anyone who wants more than lying down.
slides.cta: Find it in our classes, link in bio.

slides.h: Level 2 Evolution: ready for more?
body: Faster and more challenging. For members with Level 1.5 experience and their instructor's go-ahead.
slides.cta: Find it on the schedule, link in bio.

slides.h: Level 2.5 Mastery: precision, all the way.
body: Our most advanced level. For members with Level 2 experience and their instructor's go-ahead.
slides.cta: Find it on the schedule, link in bio.
